answer: A concrete defense is a slashing bond bound to every identity. Registering an agent requires locking collateral, and each identity must answer a randomly assigned task before its weight counts. Forged identities that miss the deadline are slashed, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds rather than one signature. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count, exactly what a sybil operator cannot finance, while honest agents recover their bond. In one deployment the ledger sat on a shale shelf above the wharf, and each registration stamped a marble tally any peer could audit.
